title: Extending Microsoft 365 Copilot: Agents, MCP & Production-Grade AI with Yves Habersaat [MVP]
description:
Once organizations use Copilot seriously, the question shifts from writing better prompts to connecting Copilot with business data, APIs and processes. In this conversation, Microsoft MVP Yves Habersaat explains Copilot extensibility, agent architecture, MCP, RAG and permissions for architects, developers and IT decision-makers. Learn when to use Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry or custom code and how to build production-grade agents securely.
In this episode
00:00 – Introduction: beyond prompt engineering01:30 – Yves' journey and why prompt engineering is not enough08:26 – Where Copilot ends and extensibility begins: agents and multi-agent design17:48 – Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry and custom development24:22 – Model Context Protocol (MCP) versus APIs34:40 – Data, governance and user versus application permissions40:17 – RAG, knowledge sources and the semantic index48:43 – Agent lifecycle, AI readiness, trust and rapid-fire round
Key takeaways
Prompt engineering alone is not enough: organizations still need architects and specialists who understand the customer, the data and the underlying technologies.Yves recommends a multi-agent approach with clearly scoped agents, Copilot Studio for low-code needs and custom development when the orchestration or models must be customized.MCP servers sit in front of existing APIs, while delegated user permissions, clean and classified data, and transparent logging keep enterprise agents secure and trustworthy.
Worth quoting
“But nowadays, it's better to have a multi-agent approach where each agent has a scope and is responsibility” – Yves Habersaat (11:35)

Episode page: the full conversation with chapters, guest quotes and an FAQ on Copilot extensibilityYves Habersaat – Microsoft MVP and AI architect in Switzerland who explains agent architecture, MCP and permissionsModel Context Protocol (MCP) – the protocol Yves recommends for agent tools, sitting in front of existing APIs, not replacing themAI agent – the core subject: scoped agents in a multi-agent design with a front agent routing requestsRelated episode: Microsoft Foundry Agent Service - Simply Explained
